lesson_title: Half a Tonne From One Hand
hook_text: Push 150 newtons on a plunger the size of a coin and the ram presses with 3 750. One equation does it.
clip_script: A hydraulic press: small pump cylinder, big ram, oil between. Same pressure both sides, so force over area here equals force over area there. F1 over A1 equals F2 over A2. Push 150 newtons on 4 square centimetres, ram of 100: 150 times 100 over 4, 3 750 newtons. Twenty-five times the area, twenty-five times the force. Need the pushing force instead? Lift 1 200 kilograms, 12 000 newtons, ram 60, pump 3: 12 000 times 3 over 60, 600 newtons. Check every time: big area, big force. Mass times 10 for newtons. Same area units both sides. That is how a mechanic presses out a bearing, a factory stamps a car door, and a brickyard squeezes clay.
visual_style: Whiteboard press frame with two cylinders; pressure arrows equal in both; the equation with numbers dropping in; a tick for the check.
pacing: The machine, the equation, two worked examples, the check.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and size a ram to lift your family car with a 100 newton push.
